items.description: Pressing the shortcut for the next ticket while the cursor is in the reply editor types a character instead of moving on. The old interface accepted a modifier combination in every context, and the new editor captures keys before the global handler sees them. Register the shortcut on the capture phase when a modifier is held and leave plain keys to the editor. Also check the shortcut on the non-English keyboard layouts the team uses, since the modifier combination clashes with an accented character on one of them.
items.reproSteps:
1. Open the inbox and select a ticket.
2. Click into the reply box.
3. Press the next-ticket shortcut.
4. A character appears in the editor and the view does not change.

comments.body: Fixed by registering the handler on capture; plain keys still go to the editor.

items.title: CSAT surveys
items.description:
After a ticket is solved the requester receives a one-question survey asking how satisfied they were, with a five-point scale and an optional comment. The answer is attached to the ticket and to the agent who solved it, and feeds the satisfaction charts.

The survey is sent once per solved ticket, to the requester only, in the ticket's language, and a day after the solve so people have time to confirm the answer worked. It is not sent for tickets solved by a merge, for tickets created by agents on behalf of a caller unless the caller has an email address, or for requesters who have unsubscribed from surveys. A reopened ticket that is solved again keeps its original rating slot instead of sending a second request.

Responses are anonymised in the aggregate reports shown to the whole desk, but leads can open an individual response. A score of one or two creates a follow-up task for the team lead due within the hour, and the task shows the ticket, the customer's comment and the agent. The follow-up is closed with a short note saying what was done.

Surveys must be accessible: the scale works with a keyboard and screen reader, the links in the email do not require a login and the page is readable on a phone without zooming. Reports compare the response rate by channel, because chat customers answer far more often than email customers and a blended number misleads.

Survey wording belongs to the brand, within a few guard rails: one question, no leading text, and the unsubscribe link always present. Translations are provided for the languages the desk supports, and an untranslated brand falls back to English with a note to the admin.

items.title: Send the survey a day after the ticket is solved
items.description: A solved ticket schedules the survey for twenty-four hours later. If the ticket is reopened before then the survey is cancelled. The send uses the requester's language and the brand's sender address, and the link opens a page that records the answer with one click from the email. The delay is a brand setting with a minimum of one hour, because some brands solve tickets in the evening and prefer the survey to arrive the next morning.
acceptanceCriteria: The survey is scheduled for 24 hours after solving
Reopening cancels a pending survey
One click in the email records the score

items.title: CSAT request fires again when a solved ticket is reopened and re-solved
items.description:
A customer wrote in furious that they had been asked to rate their experience twice for the same problem, a few days apart. The ticket had been solved, reopened because the fix did not hold, and solved again; each solve scheduled a survey and neither checked for an earlier request.

Track the survey per ticket and reuse it. If the first request was already answered, the second solve sends nothing. If it was sent but unanswered, the reminder wording is allowed once, never a fresh survey.
items.reproSteps:
1. Solve a test ticket and wait for the survey email.
2. Reopen the ticket by replying as the customer.
3. Solve it again.
4. A second survey email arrives for the same ticket.

comments.body: Reproduced; the second solve ignores the survey table entirely.
Archived: initial idea to delete the survey row on reopen, rejected because it loses the answer.

items.title: Skip the survey for tickets solved by merging into another
items.description: A ticket merged into another is closed administratively and the customer has not been helped by that act. Customers should not be asked to rate their experience for such tickets; only the surviving ticket qualifies once it is solved. The merge action marks the source ticket as survey-exempt and the reports show how many tickets were excluded for that reason. When the surviving ticket is solved the survey goes out as usual, so the customer is still asked once about the whole problem and not once per fragment.
acceptanceCriteria: A merged source ticket never triggers a survey
Reports count tickets excluded because of a merge

items.title: Open a follow-up task for the lead on scores of one or two
items.description: Low scores create a task due within one hour for the team lead of the queue, containing a link to the ticket, the score and the customer's comment. The lead closes the task with a note, and the note is visible on the ticket so the solving agent can learn from it. Tasks escalate to the head of support if they are still open after four hours. The task title includes the score and a short excerpt of the comment, so the lead can decide from the task list whether to act first on the angriest cases.
acceptanceCriteria: Scores 1 and 2 create a task due in an hour
Closing the task needs a note
Tasks open after four hours escalate

comments.body: Four hour escalation goes to the head of support, not the lead's manager.

items.title: Survey page accessible by keyboard and screen reader
items.description: The rating control is a radio group with visible focus, labelled options and a live region announcing the saved answer. The page uses sufficient contrast, works at 200 percent zoom and does not rely on colour alone. Verify with two screen readers and add automated checks to the end-to-end suite. Include the unsubscribe page in the audit, because it is rarely tested and is the only page some customers ever see from us.
acceptanceCriteria: The scale is a labelled radio group
The saved answer is announced
The page works at 200 percent zoom

items.title: Reporting dashboards
items.description:
Leads run the desk from a handful of charts: tickets created and solved per day, backlog by age, first response and resolution time, breaches by reason and satisfaction by queue. Each chart can be filtered by brand, queue, plan, channel and agent, and every point links to the ticket list behind it.

The charts must reconcile with the SLA engine. A breach counted on the dashboard is a breach on the ticket, with the same timestamp, and the monthly finance export is generated from the same query rather than rebuilt in a spreadsheet. Disagreement between the two has caused arguments, so a daily job compares them and posts any difference to the leads' channel.

Data is refreshed every five minutes, with the time of the last refresh shown on each chart. Heavy aggregates are precomputed overnight and incremental updates apply during the day.

items.title: Backlog by age chart with drill-through to tickets
items.description: Show open tickets grouped by age bands of under a day, one to three days, three to seven days and older, stacked by queue. Clicking a segment opens the inbox with the matching filter applied. The chart excludes tickets in Pending, since they are waiting on the customer, unless the lead switches the option on. Use colours that remain distinguishable for people with colour blindness and add the count as a label on each segment for those who prefer numbers to shapes.
acceptanceCriteria: Open tickets are grouped into four age bands
Clicking a segment opens the filtered inbox
Pending tickets are excluded by default

items.title: Daily reconciliation between dashboard breaches and the SLA engine
items.description: A scheduled job recomputes breaches for the previous day from the audit trail and compares the count and ticket ids with the dashboard tables. Any difference is posted to the leads' channel with the ticket ids and the likely cause. The job also stores the result so the trend of discrepancies can be charted. Keep the comparison tolerant of tickets still in flight at midnight: anything with a change in the last ten minutes of the window is compared on the following day instead.
acceptanceCriteria: The previous day's breaches are recomputed from the audit trail
Differences are posted with ticket ids

items.title: First response time chart counts automatic replies as the first response
items.description: Median first response time looked excellent because the acknowledgement email counts as a response. The chart should consider only the first public comment by an agent, ignoring messages sent by automations and the system. Existing history needs to be recomputed, and the chart should be labelled to say what it counts. The chart legend now says first human reply, and the tooltip on each point shows how many tickets contributed so thin days are not mistaken for trends.
items.reproSteps:
1. Create a ticket by email and note the automatic acknowledgement.
2. Wait an hour before an agent replies.
3. Look at the ticket's first response time on the dashboard; it shows seconds.

comments.body: Recomputed history shows median first response moving from 40 seconds to 2.6 hours, which matches what leads expect.

items.title: Backfill first response time from the first agent comment
items.description: Write a one-off script that walks tickets in batches of five hundred and recomputes first response time from the first public comment authored by a human agent. Keep the old column for a release for comparison and drop it afterwards. Log the number of tickets whose value changed by more than an hour. Run it outside staffed hours on a replica, writing results to a new column, and swap the dashboard query only after the numbers are spot-checked against ten tickets by hand.

items.title: Export the monthly breach list for finance as CSV
items.description: Finance needs the list of breaches with ticket id, customer, plan, target, time of breach, time of resolution and reason code, for any calendar month. The export is produced from the same query as the dashboard and signed with a checksum row so changes after delivery can be spotted. The checksum row lets finance detect edits, but the file itself is not secret; it is delivered through the existing report page with the same access controls as other exports.

items.title: Customer merge and duplicates
items.description:
Customers appear twice for dull reasons: a work and a personal address, a typo, a form filled in by someone else. This feature finds likely duplicate people and tickets and gives agents a safe, reversible way to merge them.

Suggestions come from matching email domains and names, phone numbers and organisation, and they are always suggestions; an agent confirms each merge. A merge moves tickets, comments and notes to the surviving record, keeps the other address as an alias so incoming mail still matches, and writes a history entry that can be used to undo the merge within thirty days.

Ticket merges follow the same rules: the source ticket's comments are copied into the target in order with a marker, the source is closed and linked, and satisfaction surveys are suppressed for the source.

items.title: Suggest duplicate requesters by name, domain and phone
items.description: A nightly job scores pairs of requesters in the same organisation using name similarity, shared phone numbers and mail alias patterns, and lists those above a threshold under a Possible duplicates tab. Agents can dismiss a suggestion so it does not return, and dismissals are visible to other agents. Thresholds start conservative so that few false suggestions appear, and the tab shows why each pair was suggested so agents learn to trust or distrust the signals.
acceptanceCriteria: Pairs above the threshold appear in a duplicates tab
Dismissed pairs do not return

items.title: Merge requesters and keep the old address as an alias
items.description: Merging moves tickets, comments, notes and tags to the surviving requester and records the other email address as an alias, so replies sent from it are matched to the survivor. The merge screen previews counts before confirming and supports undo for thirty days from the history entry. Aliases are unique across the desk: if the address is already claimed by another requester, the merge stops and explains who holds it.
acceptanceCriteria: Tickets and notes move to the surviving requester
The old address becomes an alias
A merge can be undone for thirty days

items.title: Merging two tickets duplicates attachments in the target
items.description: After merging a ticket into another every attachment appeared twice on the target. The merge copied comments with their files and then the attachment list was rebuilt by a second pass that added the same files again. The second pass should be removed, and the copy should preserve the original upload time so the list stays in chronological order. The same defect affected inline images, which were also duplicated, so the regression test should cover both file attachments and inline content.
items.reproSteps:
1. Create two tickets, one with a PDF attached.
2. Merge the ticket with the PDF into the other.
3. Open the target; the PDF is listed twice.

comments.body: Fixed in the merge service; regression test covers inline images.

items.title: Duplicate suggestions never include requesters with a plus address
items.description: Addresses such as name+billing@example.com are normalised for matching only on the local part before the plus sign when comparing against the same domain, but the candidate query joins on the raw address, so the pair is never generated. Normalise once when storing and use the stored value in the join. Once fixed, rerun the nightly job over the whole requester table, since pairs that were never generated will not appear on their own.
items.reproSteps:
1. Create two requesters, a@example.com and a+billing@example.com.
2. Run the duplicate job manually.
3. Check the suggestions; the pair is absent.

items.title: Normalise requester email addresses once when stored
items.description: Add a normalised_email column that lowercases, trims and strips plus tags for providers known to support them, backfill it and index it. Update the duplicate suggestion and alias lookups to use it and leave the original address untouched for display and sending. Providers differ about plus tags, so keep a short list of domains where stripping is safe and leave all other addresses unchanged apart from case.

items.title: Write the undo script for requester merges
items.description: Given a merge history id, restore the moved tickets, comments and notes to the original requester, remove the alias if no other record claims it and mark the history entry as undone. Run it in a transaction and refuse if the survivor has since been merged again. Write the script so it can run in dry-run mode first and print the objects it would restore; support staff will use it on real customer records.

items.title: Experiment with automatic sentiment tagging of incoming tickets
items.description: Try a small classifier that tags incoming messages as calm, frustrated or angry so leads can prioritise. The first experiment is offline only, comparing its labels with agent judgement on five hundred past tickets. If agreement is poor the idea is dropped; nothing is shown to customers or agents until the numbers justify it. Record the agreement figures per language, because a classifier that works well in English can be unusable in others, and the desk serves several languages.

comments.body: Dropped for now: the team does not want sentiment labels shown to agents.

items.title: Retire the legacy macro importer
items.description: The old importer reads macros from a CSV export of the previous help desk. All brands have been migrated, so the importer, its tests and the admin page can be deleted. Keep the migration notes in the wiki. Before removing the code, check the access logs to confirm nobody has opened the admin page in ninety days, and delete the stored upload files in the same release.

items.title: Spam review queue for borderline messages
items.description: Messages scoring between the review and discard thresholds land in a queue where a lead can release them as tickets or confirm them as spam. The queue shows the sender, subject, score and the reason the filter gave. Released messages train the filter's allow-list for the sender. Messages in the queue are kept for fourteen days and then deleted, so spam cannot accumulate without limit and personal data is not held longer than needed.
